reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, mu any probability measure on E, and S=NNReal times E times Nat times E^Nat. For any measurable a:S to R positive at every state, and any nonnegative threshold B, define F((b,u,k,h),y)=(b+1/a(s),(b*u+y/a(s))/(b+1/a(s)),k+1,h_y), where h_y(0)=y and h_y(m+1)=h(m). Vector division means reciprocal scalar multiplication. There exist Markov kernels T,H:S to E. For every state s=(b,u,k,h), T(s) is mu normalized by the density exp(-b*norm(x-u)^2/2), and H(s) is the actual law of X+sqrt(a(s))*Z under T(s) times an independent centered identity-covariance Gaussian. The square root is the standard-deviation scale.
For these same T,H and every pair of Markov kernels Q,L:S to E, there exist a Markov P:S to S and a sequence of Markov kernels R_n:S to E. At every state, P(s)=dirac s if B<=b, and otherwise P(s) is the F(s,.) pushforward of Q(s). R_0=L. For all n,s, R_(n+1)(s)=L(s) if B<=b, and otherwise it is the bind of Q(s) under y to R_n(F(s,y)). On every measurable event A this bind integrates R_n(F(s,y))(A). For every n and stopped state B<=b, R_n(s)=L(s).
For every finite n, define the history kernel kappa_k(path)=P(path(k)) on paths indexed by 0 through k. Start with the singleton path at s, append states through time n using partialTraj(kappa,0,n), and project to coordinate n. Composing this endpoint kernel with L equals R_n. This explicitly includes precomposition with the singleton initial path and pushforward by the final-coordinate map. If Q=H and L=T, then R_n=T as kernels for every n.
The quantifier order is all E,mu,a with their structures and assumptions, then all nonnegative thresholds, then existence of T,H, then all Markov Q,L, then existence of P and a single sequence R satisfying all identities for every n. The same T,H precede Q,L; P,R can depend on Q,L. The variance a can depend on every state coordinate. Equality with the threshold is a stopped state. No threshold-hitting claim, infinite-horizon limit, positive threshold lower bound, positive dimension or moment assumption on mu is asserted. There are no unspecified numerical constants; update coefficients are explicit in b,a(s),u,y.
